messages:
sam: Heads-up — after enabling the 4-bit kernels behind the feature flag on the continuous batcher, we've got a reproducible throughput regression on short sequences (~64 tokens). Rough numbers: p50 throughput down ~12%, p99 latency up ~60ms. Anyone else see this?

rahul: Saw the nightly run too. Regression only shows up when batcher pads up to the next tile boundary (tile_size=48 in our config). Long sequences are fine.

maria: Quick profiler dump I ran on the canary: kernel selection is picking the FP8 fallback for many batches that are small but rounded up by the batcher. That increases kernel_time from ~1.2ms to ~2.9ms on the matmul hotpath. Attached snippet:
```
# perf summary (sample)
batcher.pad_waste: 34%
selector.chosen: fp8_fallback (46%)
kernel_time_ms: avg 2.7 (baseline 1.15)
cpu_sys_pct: 12% -> 21%
kv_memcpy_ops: 780/s
```

devon: Interesting — I think the combination of small seqs + quantization calibration thresholds is causing our kernel-shape classifier to round up to an unsupported tile, forcing a slower path. Also seeing KV cache misalignment: when padding causes sequence_len to cross cache stripe boundary we do a memcpy every step.

sam: Do you have the exact command to repro? I want to run with profiler locally.

maria: Repro command I used:
```
./run_infer --model redwood-mix-3b --quant=4 --batcher=continuous --tile_size=48 --seq_len=64 --warmup=50 --iters=200
# then collect perf: ./tools/trace_collect --pid $PID --events cpu,kern,memcopy
```

perf-bot: Canary results uploaded: s3://redwood-ci/canaries/1967890123/
Summary CSV: throughput_rps,lat_p50_ms,lat_p99_ms,pad_waste_pct
values: 182.4, 18.6, 142.3, 33.8

rahul: Two hypotheses: (1) selector quantization calibration bins are coarser for 4-bit and map many shapes to fallback; (2) continuous-batcher rounds up to tile boundaries that are not friendly to our packed 4-bit kernels so we hit memcpy/reshape slow path. Either one could explain CPU spike.

devon: I instrumented kvcache and saw per-step memcpy hotspots when (seq_len % stripe) > 0. Example stack: memcpy -> kv_realign -> token_step. That was ~0.6ms extra per token on these small batches.

maria: Proposed quick mitigations:
- change batcher tile quantization to prefer smaller tile (ceil-to-16 instead of 32) for quant=4 workloads
- add a selector override: prefer int8 kernel when pad_waste > 25% to avoid fp8 fallback
- delay 4-bit rollout on continuous-batcher until selector calibration refined

sam: Any downsides to ceil-to-16? Might increase kernel_count (more variants) and reduce packing efficiency for long sequences.

maria: Tradeoff: more kernel variants, slightly worse long-seq perf in exchange for huge win for PLG small seq tail. We can gate per-customer.

rahul: I ran a microbench: changing tile quant from 32->16 recovers ~9% throughput and cuts pad_waste to 18%. Numbers:
```
config A (tile=48, quant4): throughput 182 rps, pad_waste 33.8%
config B (tile=16, quant4): throughput 198 rps, pad_waste 18.1%
kernel_path percent: fp8_fallback 46% -> 12%
```

devon: Also tried a temporary kvcache alignment fix (align slab_start to 64B) — reduced memcpy ops by 84% and lowered cpu_sys to baseline. Patch in my branch dev/fix-kv-align.

sam: Nice. Can we run combined (tile=16 + kv-align) in canary? If that recovers regression we can roll a hotfix.

ci-bot: Deploy queued: canary group=small-seq-cases image=dev/fix-kv-align+tile16 expected_duration 45m

maria: Longer term: we should add a selector telemetry metric that captures quantized-shape -> kernel mapping counts so we can automatically detect shape-coverage holes. Also add a pad-waste estimator in the optimizer so routing policy can prefer int8 when pad_waste predicted > threshold.

rahul: Agree. Action items:
- dev/fix-kv-align PR (devon) -> merge after perf run (TODAY)
- batcher tile fallback policy (maria) -> prototype config change + canary (tomorrow)
- selector telemetry (rahul) -> instrument and create dashboard (this week)

sam: Thanks all. I'll monitor alerts and rollback if any negative impact on long-seq customers. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: Created perf ticket PERF-2218: "quant4 continuous-batcher pad-waste regression" and attached traces.

devon: I'll upload my heap/profile to the ticket and push the canary results when done.

sam: Closing loop here once canary finishes. If anybody finds contradictory numbers ping me directly.
